summary:
LUNA-VIEW is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to simplify the evaluation and comparison of potential landing sites near the Moon's south pole. Lunar missions face challenges due to extreme variations in sunlight availability and limited direct communication with Earth. Even small changes in landing location or date can significantly affect mission operations.

LUNA-VIEW brings essential mission-planning information into one intuitive application. Users can explore lunar landing locations, select mission dates, and visualize Sun and Earth positions relative to the lunar horizon.

Key features include interactive 3D lunar exploration, solar illumination analysis, Earth visibility and communication window tracking, dynamic mission timelines, and side-by-side landing site comparisons. It also aims to provide mission suitability assessments and AI-powered insights to help users evaluate alternative scenarios.

By transforming complex astronomical and geographical data into clear visualizations, LUNA-VIEW helps users understand how changes in landing locations and dates affect power generation and communication opportunities. It aims to support informed mission planning while making lunar exploration more accessible to researchers, educators, students, and the public.
details:
LUNA-VIEW

Lunar Landing Site Intelligence & Mission Planning System

Live Project: https://luna-view-frontend.vercel.app/

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/renuasmitha/Luna-View

Project Overview

LUNA-VIEW is an interactive web-based platform designed to simplify the evaluation and comparison of potential landing sites near the Moon's south pole. It addresses two major challenges in lunar mission planning: extreme and rapidly changing solar illumination conditions and limited direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

The platform brings essential astronomical information into one intuitive interface, allowing users to explore potential lunar landing locations, select mission dates, visualize the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local lunar horizon, and compare environmental conditions across different mission scenarios.

What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

LUNA-VIEW combines astronomical calculations, interactive visualizations, and mission comparison capabilities to help users understand changing lunar surface conditions.

Its key capabilities include:

1. Interactive Lunar Explorer

Allows users to explore potential lunar landing locations, examine candidate sites, and work with geographical coordinates to investigate different lunar regions.

2. Sun Position Intelligence

Visualizes solar elevation and estimates sunlight availability at selected locations. Users can examine how illumination conditions change over time and identify potentially useful sunlight windows for mission planning.

3. Earth Communication Tracker

Tracks Earth's apparent position relative to the local lunar horizon and identifies periods of geometric Earth visibility. This helps users understand potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

4. Mission Timeline Simulator

Provides a time-based view of changing Sun and Earth positions. Users can explore how environmental conditions evolve throughout a selected mission period.

5. Mission Comparison Centre

Enables side-by-side comparison of different landing locations and mission dates, helping users understand trade-offs between solar illumination and Earth visibility.

6. Mission Rescheduling

Helps explore alternative landing dates and locations when mission schedules change due to delays or technical constraints.

The backend uses NASA/JPL Horizons for astronomical ephemeris calculations, with an analytical fallback model when the external data service is unavailable.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNA-VIEW aims to reduce the complexity of evaluating lunar landing scenarios by presenting important astronomical information through accessible visualizations and comparative analysis.

It can help users:

  • Understand solar illumination patterns at different landing locations.
  • Identify potential Earth visibility and communication windows.
  • Compare alternative landing sites and mission dates.
  • Explore the impact of mission schedule changes.
  • Understand the relationship between sunlight availability and communication opportunities.

Beyond mission planning, the platform can serve as an educational resource for students, educators, researchers, and the general public, making complex astronomical concepts easier to explore.

Tools and Technologies

The project uses:

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Astronomical Data: NASA/JPL Horizons API
  • Scientific Computation: Python-based analytical calculations
  • Deployment: Vercel
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub

The architecture separates frontend visualization from backend calculations, allowing the platform to retrieve astronomical time-series data through API endpoints.

Creativity and Innovation

The innovation behind LUNA-VIEW lies in bringing lunar exploration, astronomical visualization, temporal analysis, and mission comparison together in a single accessible platform.

Instead of requiring users to navigate multiple complex scientific tools, LUNA-VIEW provides an integrated environment where changing a landing location or mission date reveals how important operational conditions change.

Its focus on both solar illumination and Earth visibility highlights the trade-offs involved in lunar mission planning. A location with favourable sunlight conditions may not necessarily offer equally favourable Earth visibility, making comparative analysis particularly valuable.

Factors Considered

The project considers several important factors affecting preliminary lunar mission planning:

  • Solar elevation and illumination availability.
  • Earth's apparent elevation and geometric visibility.
  • Potential communication opportunities.
  • Mission dates and timeline variations.
  • Differences between candidate landing locations.
  • Data availability and calculation accuracy.
  • Accessibility and clarity of scientific visualizations.

LUNA-VIEW also emphasizes scientific transparency. Geometric Earth visibility does not guarantee an actual communication link, and sunlight availability does not directly represent electrical power generation. Actual mission conditions would also depend on terrain, equipment, antenna orientation, and other operational constraints.

Our Ultimate Vision

Our ultimate vision is to make lunar mission planning more accessible, interactive, and understandable by transforming complex astronomical information into meaningful visual insights.

LUNA-VIEW aims to evolve into a comprehensive lunar mission decision-support platform by incorporating validated lunar terrain and illumination datasets, more detailed environmental analysis, and advanced mission-planning capabilities.

By connecting scientific data with intuitive technology, we hope to contribute to a future where exploring and understanding the Moon becomes easier for researchers, students, and everyone interested in space exploration.

LUNA-VIEW is an independent educational and decision-support project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It is not an official NASA product and is not endorsed or validated by NASA.
